title: How Do Satellites Get to Space?

cues.text: Satellites do not simply fly into space by themselves.
Most human-made satellites are carried into space by rockets.
A rocket produces thrust by expelling gas at high speed.
This force pushes the rocket in the opposite direction.
Launching a satellite requires enormous energy.
The rocket must carry the spacecraft above much of Earth’s atmosphere and give it the right speed and direction for its intended orbit.
Once a stage has used its fuel, it can separate so that the remaining rocket carries less mass.
When the spacecraft reaches the required conditions, it can be released into its planned orbit.
The satellite then uses its onboard systems to operate, communicate, and carry out its mission.
Not every satellite follows the same route.
Some are released directly into orbit by a rocket.
Others may be transported to a space station and deployed from there.
Once in orbit, the satellite still needs monitoring and control from the ground.
Engineers check its health and help ensure that it performs its intended tasks.

transcript: Satellites do not simply fly into space by themselves. Most human-made satellites are carried into space by rockets.
A rocket produces thrust by expelling gas at high speed. This force pushes the rocket in the opposite direction.
Launching a satellite requires enormous energy. The rocket must carry the spacecraft above much of Earth’s atmosphere and give it the right speed and direction for its intended orbit.
Many rockets have multiple stages. Once a stage has used its fuel, it can separate so that the remaining rocket carries less mass.
When the spacecraft reaches the required conditions, it can be released into its planned orbit. The satellite then uses its onboard systems to operate, communicate, and carry out its mission.
Not every satellite follows the same route. Some are released directly into orbit by a rocket. Others may be transported to a space station and deployed from there.
Once in orbit, the satellite still needs monitoring and control from the ground. Engineers check its health and help ensure that it performs its intended tasks.
